Day 1
From Hotel: 10 min · 12 min → Ponts Couverts
1. Ponts Couverts
A line of three medieval bridges guarded by four square watchtowers, survivors of Strasbourg's old ramparts at the western tip of the Grande Île. The towers and weirs frame the canals of Petite France — the classic view is from the terrace of the Barrage Vauban just behind them.
Read more
Open 24/7
~30 min
Place du Quartier Blanc · Petite France
3 min · 2 min → MAMCS – Musée d'Art Moderne et Contemporain
2. MAMCS – Musée d'Art Moderne et Contemporain
Strasbourg's museum of modern and contemporary art in a glass-and-steel building on the Ill near the Ponts Couverts. Its permanent collection covers 18,400 works from 1870 to the present — paintings, sculpture, graphic art, photography, and design.
Read more
Tuesday - Sunday 10:00am - 6:00pm
Closed Monday
~1 hr 30 min
1 Place Hans Jean Arp · Petite France
7 min · 2 min → La Petite France
3. La Petite France
The most picturesque quarter of the Grande Île — a maze of cobbled lanes and canals lined with half-timbered tanners' and millers' houses, their steep roofs once used for drying hides. Flower-decked bridges and waterside terraces make it Strasbourg's postcard.
Read more
Open 24/7
~45 min
Place Benjamin Zix · Petite France
5 min · 17 min → hotel
Day 2
From Hotel: 18 min · 5 min → Église Saint-Paul
1. Église Saint-Paul
A soaring neo-Gothic church of pink Vosges sandstone, built as the garrison church for the German imperial army. Its twin 76-metre spires rise straight from the river Ill on the tip of an island, mirrored in the water — one of the Neustadt's most photographed silhouettes.
Read more
Open 24/7
~20 min
Place du Général Eisenhower · Neustadt
6 min · 2 min → Place de la République
2. Place de la République
The monumental centrepiece of the Neustadt, the German imperial quarter now UNESCO-listed alongside the Grande Île. A circular garden of ginkgo and magnolia is ringed by grand Wilhelmine palaces — the Palais du Rhin, the National Library, and the Théâtre National.
Read more
Open 24/7
~30 min
Place de la République · Neustadt
22 min · 6 min → Parc de l'Orangerie
3. Parc de l'Orangerie
Strasbourg's oldest and largest park, landscaped around the Pavillon Joséphine. Shaded alleys lead to a lake with rowing boats, a waterfall, and a free-roaming stork enclosure — the bird that has been Alsace's emblem for centuries. A green finish beside the European quarter.
Read more

~1 hr
Avenue de l'Europe · Orangerie
15 min · 5 min → Batorama Boat Tour
4. Batorama Boat Tour
A 70-minute cruise on the river Ill — the classic way to see Strasbourg. Glass-roofed boats leave the Palais Rohan landing, drop through the lock of Petite France, and glide past the German-era Neustadt and the European institutions, with multilingual audio commentary throughout.

Day 3
From Hotel: 6 min · 10 min → Strasbourg Cathedral
1. Strasbourg Cathedral
One of the great Gothic cathedrals of Europe. Its single 142-metre spire made it the tallest building in the world for over two centuries, and the carved west front, rose window, and Renaissance astronomical clock are unmissable. A 332-step climb reaches the rooftop platform over the Grande Île.
Read more
Cathedral Platform · 4.7 · visitstrasbourg.fr
Daily 9:30am - 1:00pm · 1:30pm - 7:15pm
~1 hr
Place de la Cathédrale · Grande Île
1 min · 2 min → Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame
2. Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame
A museum of Upper Rhenish art from the early Middle Ages to 1681, housed in Gothic and Renaissance buildings at the foot of the cathedral. Holdings include original cathedral sculptures, medieval stained glass, goldwork, and the portal figures of Ecclesia and Synagoga.
Read more
Tuesday - Sunday 10:00am - 6:00pm
Closed Monday
~1 hr 30 min
3 Place du Château · Grande Île
1 min · 2 min → Palais Rohan
3. Palais Rohan
An 18th-century episcopal palace built between 1731 and 1742 for the prince-bishops of Strasbourg. It houses three museums — the Musée Archéologique, the Musée des Arts Décoratifs with royal apartments, and the Musée des Beaux-Arts with European paintings from Giotto to El Greco.
Read more
Wednesday - Monday 10:00am - 6:00pm
Closed Tuesday
~1 hr 30 min
2 Place du Château · Grande Île
3 min · 2 min → Musée Alsacien
4. Musée Alsacien
A museum of Alsatian folk culture in 17th-century half-timbered houses on the Quai Saint-Nicolas. Galleries cover daily life across rural and urban Alsace — furniture, ceramics, textiles, toys, and traditional interiors reconstructed across three linked courtyards.
Read more
Wednesday - Monday 10:00am - 6:00pm

~1 hr
23 Quai Saint-Nicolas · Grande Île
7 min · 2 min → Place Kléber
5. Place Kléber
Strasbourg's largest square and civic heart, ringed by elegant facades and anchored by the neoclassical Aubette. A statue of the Strasbourg-born General Kléber stands at its centre, and in summer the open plaza fills with cafés, markets, and events.

Day 4
From Hotel: 12 min · 13 min → Barrage Vauban
1. Barrage Vauban
A 17th-century weir designed by Vauban to flood the plain in case of siege. The structure shelters a gallery of medieval cathedral sculptures. Its rooftop terrace gives the classic panoramic view over the Ponts Couverts and the Petite France rooftops.
Read more
Daily 9:00am - 7:30pm
~45 min
Rooftop terrace currently closed for renovation — check locally before visiting
Promenade Vauban · Petite France
30 min · 8 min → Palais du Rhin
2. Palais du Rhin
A monumental Wilhelmine palace on Place de la République, completed in 1889 as the imperial residence for Kaiser Wilhelm II. Its neo-Renaissance sandstone facade anchors the Neustadt, listed alongside the Grande Île as a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Read more
Open 24/7
~20 min
Interior not open to the public — exterior only
2 Place de la République · Neustadt
10 min → European Parliament
3. European Parliament Visitors' Centre
The Louise Weiss building is the main seat of the European Parliament, where MEPs vote during monthly plenary sessions. The visitor centre covers the EU's history and workings, and visitors can observe the hemicycle from the public gallery during session weeks or via guided access outside them.
Read more
Monday - Thursday 9:00am - 5:00pm · Friday 9:00am - 12:00pm
Closed Saturday & Sunday
~1 hr
Free
Timed slot required — book in advance via the official visitor site
Allée du Printemps · European Quarter
12 min → Palais Universitaire
4. Palais Universitaire
The main building of the University of Strasbourg, built between 1879 and 1884 under the German imperial administration. Its neo-Renaissance sandstone facade on Place de l'Université is one of the Neustadt's key landmarks, flanked by lecture halls and the main university library.
Read more
Open 24/7
~30 min
Grounds and main entrance are exterior access only — interior requires university affiliation

Local Tastes
Tarte Flambée
Ultra-thin wood-fired flatbread topped with crème fraîche, raw onions, and smoked lardons — Alsace's signature shareable dish, eaten in successive rounds.
La Binchstub · Le Tire-Bouchon
Choucroute Garnie
Sauerkraut braised in white wine and piled with salted pork cuts, sausages, and potatoes — the hearty winstub classic of Alsace.
Winstub Le Clou · Chez Yvonne
Baeckeoffe
A one-pot casserole of pork, beef, and lamb marinated overnight then slow-cooked with potatoes, onions, and white wine in a sealed terrine.
Chez Yvonne · Le Tire-Bouchon
Kougelhopf
Tall fluted brioche studded with raisins and almonds and dusted with sugar — the iconic Alsatian sweet, traditionally baked for Sunday breakfast.
Au Fond du Jardin · Maison Alsacienne de Biscuiterie
Food Delivery
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted.
Good coverage across Strasbourg's city centre, Grande Île and the Krutenau quarter; strong on international and fast-casual options alongside French classics. Reliable for hotel delivery within 25–35 minutes on most central routes.
ubereats.com
Deliveroo
Foreign number: not required. — sign-up runs on Google, Apple, Facebook or email with no phone field at all, so no verification code has to arrive.
Well-regarded UK-founded platform with a curated restaurant selection in Strasbourg; tends toward mid-range brasseries, sushi spots and popular local chains. Useful for evenings when returning late from a day trip to the Vosges.
deliveroo.fr
Just Eat
Foreign number: not required. — the account is made with Google, Facebook or an email address — there is no phone field, so no code has to arrive.
Large restaurant aggregator with broad coverage across Strasbourg and the surrounding Bas-Rhin area; restaurant variety is wide, covering Alsatian tarte flambée, pizzerias and fast food alongside more formal dining. A practical backup option when the other platforms show limited availability.
just-eat.fr

Day Trips by Train
Sélestat · 25 min
Historic Renaissance town with one of Europe's great humanist libraries and the gateway to the hilltop Haut-Koenigsbourg castle and the Wine Route villages.
book at: SNCF Connect or Omio
Colmar · 30 min
Storybook Alsatian town with pastel half-timbered houses and the Little Venice canals — the classic Alsace day trip, an easy half-hour down the line.
book at: SNCF Connect or Omio
Obernai · 30 min
A walled wine town on the Route des Vins — ramparts, a belfry, and a market square of flower-decked Alsatian houses, all a short walk to the old centre.
book at: SNCF Connect or Omio
Baden-Baden · Germany · 45 min
Elegant Black Forest spa town across the Rhine — thermal baths, belle-époque promenades, and a famous casino, an easy hop over the border.
book at: SNCF Connect or Omio
Basel · Switzerland · 1 hr 20 min
Rhine-side Swiss city with a renowned art scene — the Kunstmuseum and Fondation Beyeler — and a medieval old town wrapped around the river.
book at: SNCF Connect or Omio

Heads Up
Barrage Vauban — Terrace Closed
The Vauban Dam's panoramic rooftop terrace is closed for a major renovation.
Astronomical Clock — No Sunday Show
The cathedral's astronomical-clock procession runs once a day at 12:30pm but not on Sundays when mass is celebrated.
Strasbourg Museums — Closed Tuesday
The city's municipal museums including the Palais Rohan museums and the Museum of Modern Art all close on Tuesdays.
Worth Knowing

A City Between Two Worlds

Strasbourg has spent its whole history on a seam. Its cathedral spire was the tallest structure on Earth for well over two centuries, and beneath it Gutenberg spent his Strasbourg years tinkering with the movable type that would remake the world — a fitting birthplace for a city that has always been a crossing point of ideas as much as of rivers.

What makes the two days fit together is the layering. Day 1 is the French Grande Île — half-timbered, intimate, medieval. Day 2 is the Neustadt, the monumental quarter Germany built to stamp its own grandeur onto the city. UNESCO now lists them together, two empires' visions of the same place side by side, which is why the European Parliament chose Strasbourg as its seat: a city fought over so often it became the natural home for reconciliation.
